correctness.rationale: First three order-three moment equations give c1=1/2−sqrt(q/(12p)), c2=1/2+sqrt(p/(12q)), p∈[1/4,3/4]. PSD gives M11=2pa11−p²≥0, so a12=c1−a11≤−f(p). The derivative of f changes sign once when p³(1−p)=1/12 (strict monotonicity on this interval). The explicit A_p with diagonals p/2 and q/2 has M=0 and satisfies fourth order-three condition b^TAc=1/6, hence attains bound. At equality PSD and e^TMe=0 force all M=0 and unique A. Independently numerically solved p*=0.5861069554217851, δ=0.03563906993888327 and checked moment/order/symplectic matrix residual ≤6e−17. Finite check supplements all-parameter inequality.
residual_risks: Requires two stages and normalized stage abscissas; without these assumptions quantitative bound may fail.

final_claim: Among real two-stage classical-order>=3 RK methods with positive weights, 0<=c1<c2<=1, and algebraic-stability matrix M=BA+A^TB−bb^T PSD, the sharp least maximum negative Butcher entry is δ*=sqrt((1−p*)/(12p*))−(1−p*)/2≈0.03563906994, where p*∈(1/4,3/4) uniquely solves p*³(1−p*)=1/12, attained by a unique symplectic tableau up to stage permutation.
limitations: Only exactly two stages, positive b, c within normalized step
